callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. `js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js` now parses the fa per-segment ledger line (`fa-tokens: {...}`) that fa emits since gh-1241, so the dashboard token-spend panels fill from real data instead of staying empty. Old `CommandLineUtils` parsing is untouched.

- Dashboard: new **Source** column in Recent Runs — green badge for `reported`, dashed amber badge + tinted row for `estimated`; both CSVs gain a `source` column.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.

Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.

The `$` anchor requires the match to end at the end of the line (minus trailing whitespace). Since `(\{.*\})` must end with `}` immediately before `\s*$`, greedy matching takes the last `}` that allows the whole pattern to match. If the line is `prefix fa-tokens: {"a":1} garbage` — no match since after last `}` there's " garbage" which doesn't match `\s*$`. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];

Findings to consider:

1. **Regex `/fa-tokens:\s*(\{.*\})\s*$/`** — greedy `.*` with `$` anchor. On a line like `fa-tokens: {...} some trailing text` it won't match (good). But greedy `.*` matches to the LAST `}` on the line — if the JSON contains a nested `}` followed by trailing text... The `$` anchor requires the match to end at the end of the line (minus trailing whitespace). Since `(\{.*\})` must end with `}` immediately before `\s*$`, greedy matching takes the last `}` that allows the whole pattern to match. If the line is `prefix fa-tokens: {"a":1} garbage` — no match since after last `}` there's " garbage" which doesn't match `\s*$`. But wait: greedy backtracks — it could try `{"a":1}` and then require `\s*$` — " garbage" fails. So no match. Fine.

   Edge case: a line with TWO fa-tokens JSON payloads? Unlikely. Also a log line where the fa-tokens JSON appears mid-line with a timestamp prefix — `.*$` handles prefix fine. What about a line where fa-tokens JSON is followed by something else on the same line from log interleaving? Would be skipped silently. Acceptable.

   Edge: JSON containing `}` inside string values, e.g. `"sessionId":"a}b"`. Greedy takes to last `}` which would be the string's closing... actually last `}` in the line is the final one if valid JSON. Fine for typical shapes.

   More subtle: `fa-tokens:` appearing in the middle of a longer JSON-like line where the captured group starts at the first `{` — greedy `.*` would swallow to the last `}` and JSON.parse could fail (returning null → returns null → tokens sample lost). E.g., a wrapper `{"msg":"fa-tokens: {...}"}` — the regex would match `fa-tokens: ` then capture `{...}"}` — the greedy match from the first `{` after `fa-tokens: `... Hmm, `text.match(/fa-tokens:\s*(\{.*\})\s*$/)` requires `fa-tokens:` then optional whitespace then `{`, and end at line end. In a wrapper line, after `{...}` there'd be `"}` at the end — `(\{.*\})` greedy takes everything from first `{` to last `}` at the line end, which would be the wrapper's closing brace, producing invalid JSON → parseJson returns null → return null. Then falls through? No — `return null` inside the `if (faMatch)` block. So a wrapped fa-tokens line yields null and the old `Tokens` check is skipped. Minor robustness issue, worth a suggestion at most. Actually it returns null and never reaches the CommandLineUtils branch — slight behavioral quirk. Low severity.

2. **`parseInt(payload.input, 10) || 0`** — if input is a float like 722300.5, parseInt truncates — fine. If input is a string with commas "722,300" → parseInt gives 722 — the old branch has parseNumberWithSuffix handling commas. fa emits raw numbers presumably. Minor.

3. **requests merging change**: Old code: `samples.push(Object.assign({ attemptIndex: samples.length + 1 }, lastRequests || {}, tokens));` — lastRequests always merged (stale metadata concern). New: `if (tokens.requests == null && lastRequests)` — but fa branch ALWAYS sets `requests: parseInt(...) || 0`, so tokens.requests is never null for fa lines. For CommandLineUtils branch, tokens.requests is undefined → merged. OK matches PR description.

   But wait — there's a subtle bug: for the fa branch, `requests: parseInt(payload.requests, 10) || 0` means if requests is missing it's 0, and `tokens.requests == null` is false (it's 0), so no merge. Fine.

4. **Dedup by (sessionId, segment) with `parseInt(payload.segment, 10) || 0`**: If segment is missing/0 for multiple lines of the same sessionId, all collapse to `session:0` and only first counted. Also if fa emits `segment:0` legitimately... Dedup keyed only on faSessionId when segment missing → repeated lines with same sessionId and no segment get dropped. Acceptable given the ledger format always has segment.

   More important: `faSegment: parseInt(payload.segment, 10) || 0` — a payload with segment legitimately 0 vs missing is indistinguishable. Minor.

If the same fa-tokens line legitimately appears in two jobs (e.g. setup job and main job echo the same ledger), dedup drops the second. That's the intent ("replayed"). OK.

   What about a run with TWO different fa sessions (resume creates new session? no — resume-aware means same sessionId, segment N increments). OK.

Mixed old+fa → only fa sources counted, source could be 'reported' even though some samples are old-style. Acceptable-ish. But note: aggregate `source` for a run mixing old and new would say 'reported' which is fine.

6. **HTML**: `sourceBadge` uses htmlEscape(r.source) — good. `sortAttr(r.source || '')` escaped. OK.

7. **CSV**: `source` column added before `url`. Backward compat: consumers parsing CSV positionally would break, but CSV is header-based. Fine. Note: cache — the usage cache stores `row` objects without `source` for older cached entries; when rendering from cache, old rows just have empty source. Fine.

Wait no — `return null` inside the `if (faMatch)` block — the function returns null entirely, skipping old parsing. Is that right? A malformed fa-tokens line would be ignored rather than parsed by the old branch. The old branch requires "Tokens" substring anyway; "fa-tokens:" contains "tokens" but `indexOf('Tokens')` is case-sensitive — 'fa-tokens' lowercase wouldn't match 'Tokens'. So old branch wouldn't parse it anyway. Fine.

15. **`rawTokensLine: text.trim()`** — includes full JSON. Fine.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.

Tests pass (1583/0). Now let me do a thorough review.

Findings to consider:

1. **Regex `/fa-tokens:\s*(\{.*\})\s*$/`** — greedy `.*` with `$` anchor. On a line like `fa-tokens: {...} some trailing text` it won't match (good). But greedy `.*` matches to the LAST `}` on the line — if the JSON contains a nested `}` followed by trailing text... The `$` anchor requires the match to end at the end of the line (minus trailing whitespace). Since `(\{.*\})` must end with `}` immediately before `\s*$`, greedy matching takes the last `}` that allows the whole pattern to match. If the line is `prefix fa-tokens: {"a":1} garbage` — no match since after last `}` there's " garbage" which doesn't match `\s*$`. But wait: greedy backtracks — it could try `{"a":1}` and then require `\s*$` — " garbage" fails. So no match. Fine.

   Edge case: a line with TWO fa-tokens JSON payloads? Unlikely. Also a log line where the fa-tokens JSON appears mid-line with a timestamp prefix — `.*$` handles prefix fine. What about a line where fa-tokens JSON is followed by something else on the same line from log interleaving? Would be skipped silently. Acceptable.

   Edge: JSON containing `}` inside string values, e.g. `"sessionId":"a}b"`. Greedy takes to last `}` which would be the string's closing... actually last `}` in the line is the final one if valid JSON. Fine for typical shapes.

   More subtle: `fa-tokens:` appearing in the middle of a longer JSON-like line where the captured group starts at the first `{` — greedy `.*` would swallow to the last `}` and JSON.parse could fail (returning null → returns null → tokens sample lost). E.g., a wrapper `{"msg":"fa-tokens: {...}"}` — the regex would match `fa-tokens: ` then capture `{...}"}` — the greedy match from the first `{` after `fa-tokens: `... Hmm, `text.match(/fa-tokens:\s*(\{.*\})\s*$/)` requires `fa-tokens:` then optional whitespace then `{`, and end at line end. In a wrapper line, after `{...}` there'd be `"}` at the end — `(\{.*\})` greedy takes everything from first `{` to last `}` at the line end, which would be the wrapper's closing brace, producing invalid JSON → parseJson returns null → return null. Then falls through? No — `return null` inside the `if (faMatch)` block. So a wrapped fa-tokens line yields null and the old `Tokens` check is skipped. Minor robustness issue, worth a suggestion at most. Actually it returns null and never reaches the CommandLineUtils branch — slight behavioral quirk. Low severity.

2. **`parseInt(payload.input, 10) || 0`** — if input is a float like 722300.5, parseInt truncates — fine. If input is a string with commas "722,300" → parseInt gives 722 — the old branch has parseNumberWithSuffix handling commas. fa emits raw numbers presumably. Minor.

3. **requests merging change**: Old code: `samples.push(Object.assign({ attemptIndex: samples.length + 1 }, lastRequests || {}, tokens));` — lastRequests always merged (stale metadata concern). New: `if (tokens.requests == null && lastRequests)` — but fa branch ALWAYS sets `requests: parseInt(...) || 0`, so tokens.requests is never null for fa lines. For CommandLineUtils branch, tokens.requests is undefined → merged. OK matches PR description.

   But wait — there's a subtle bug: for the fa branch, `requests: parseInt(payload.requests, 10) || 0` means if requests is missing it's 0, and `tokens.requests == null` is false (it's 0), so no merge. Fine.

4. **Dedup by (sessionId, segment) with `parseInt(payload.segment, 10) || 0`**: If segment is missing/0 for multiple lines of the same sessionId, all collapse to `session:0` and only first counted. Also if fa emits `segment:0` legitimately... Dedup keyed only on faSessionId when segment missing → repeated lines with same sessionId and no segment get dropped. Acceptable given the ledger format always has segment.

   More important: `faSegment: parseInt(payload.segment, 10) || 0` — a payload with segment legitimately 0 vs missing is indistinguishable. Minor.

   Another consideration: **dedup across multiple jobs/logs in the same run**. downloadRunLogs joins multiple jobs' logs with '\n'. If the same fa-tokens line legitimately appears in two jobs (e.g. setup job and main job echo the same ledger), dedup drops the second. That's the intent ("replayed"). OK.

   What about a run with TWO different fa sessions (resume creates new session? no — resume-aware means same sessionId, segment N increments). OK.

5. **`source` aggregation**: `faSources` collected from samples with `sample.source` truthy. Old CommandLineUtils lines have no `source` → run source = '' when only old lines. Mixed old+fa → only fa sources counted, source could be 'reported' even though some samples are old-style. Acceptable-ish. But note: aggregate `source` for a run mixing old and new would say 'reported' which is fine.

   Edge: source value not 'reported'/'estimated' (e.g. something else) → badge CSS class: `r.source === 'estimated' ? 'src-est' : 'src-rep'` — any unknown source gets green 'reported' styling. And rowClass: only 'estimated' gets tint. Minor, suggestion-level.

6. **HTML**: `sourceBadge` uses htmlEscape(r.source) — good. `sortAttr(r.source || '')` escaped. OK.

7. **CSV**: `source` column added before `url`. Backward compat: consumers parsing CSV positionally would break, but CSV is header-based. Fine. Note: cache — the usage cache stores `row` objects without `source` for older cached entries; when rendering from cache, old rows just have empty source. Fine.

   One real issue: **cache invalidation**. Cached rows (from cache.json written before this change) lack `source`, so dashboard shows blank source for them until cache refresh. Not blocking.

8. **Test in PR description claims "1583 passed / 0 failed, including 4 new tests"** — verified: 1583 passed locally. ✓

9. **Ticket AC #2**: "Aggregation: sum segments per sessionId ... do not double-count resumed segments" — the implementation dedupes by (sessionId, segment) but note the semantics: it doesn't "sum per sessionId" — it sums all samples. If the same session's segments are split across separate extract calls (one per job log), extractTokenUsage is called on the joined logs so it's fine.

   Hmm wait — there's a real potential bug: **the same sessionId could legitimately emit the same segment number in different RUNS**, but extractTokenUsage is per-run, so no cross-run contamination. Good.

   Another real one: within a run, if fa is run twice with the same sessionId resumed across... covered.

10. **`attemptIndex` after `continue` on dedup**: `attemptIndex: samples.length + 1` — consistent.

11. **`fa-tokens:` check order**: The fa branch runs before the `Tokens` substring check. If a CommandLineUtils line contained "fa-tokens:" substring it would be misrouted — very unlikely.

12. **The old-line `requests` behavior change**: Previously `lastRequests` was always merged into tokens samples (even if the tokens line had its own requests? Old tokens lines don't have requests). New condition `tokens.requests == null` — old lines have undefined requests → merge happens. Same behavior. ✓

13. **resumeStages/feedback loop** — untouched.

14. **`payload.input == null && output == null && cacheRead == null` check** — if a line has only `requests` and `source` but no token fields, returns null and does NOT fall through to the old parser (returns null from within the faMatch block). Wait no — `return null` inside the `if (faMatch)` block — the function returns null entirely, skipping old parsing. Is that right? A malformed fa-tokens line would be ignored rather than parsed by the old branch. The old branch requires "Tokens" substring anyway; "fa-tokens:" contains "tokens" but `indexOf('Tokens')` is case-sensitive — 'fa-tokens' lowercase wouldn't match 'Tokens'. So old branch wouldn't parse it anyway. Fine.

15. **`rawTokensLine: text.trim()`** — includes full JSON. Fine.

16. Test quality: The tests are decent. The IT-7 fixture test covers parsing. Aggregation test covers dedup + mixed source. Dashboard test asserts string presence. CSV test asserts header contains 'source' and body contains 'reported' — weak-ish (could false positive) but fine.

**Summary**: Correct, well-scoped implementation of gh-735 — all 4 ticket ACs are covered (fixture parse, per-segment dedup, dashboard source marking, CSV columns) and the full suite passes locally (1583/0, matching the PR claim). Old `CommandLineUtils` parsing is genuinely untouched.

Four non-blocking robustness gaps in the new fa branch: (1) the greedy `(\{.*\})$` regex plus the hard `return null` on JSON parse failure silently drops any fa-tokens line that is wrapped in a larger JSON log line, with no fallback; (2) payloads missing `segment` collapse to `0` and get deduped together, so real lines for the same session could be dropped; (3) any `source` value other than `estimated` renders as the green `reported` badge; (4) the "stale `lastRequests` no longer merged" behavior from the PR description has no test.

**Next Steps**:
1. Optional: tighten the fa-tokens regex / fall through on parse failure instead of returning null.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.

Findings to consider:

1. **Regex `/fa-tokens:\s*(\{.*\})\s*$/`** — greedy `.*` with `$` anchor. On a line like `fa-tokens: {...} some trailing text` it won't match (good). But greedy `.*` matches to the LAST `}` on the line — if the JSON contains a nested `}` followed by trailing text... The `$` anchor requires the match to end at the end of the line (minus trailing whitespace). Since `(\{.*\})` must end with `}` immediately before `\s*$`, greedy matching takes the last `}` that allows the whole pattern to match. If the line is `prefix fa-tokens: {"a":1} garbage` — no match since after last `}` there's " garbage" which doesn't match `\s*$`. But wait: greedy backtracks — it could try `{"a":1}` and then require `\s*$` — " garbage" fails. So no match. Fine.

   Edge case: a line with TWO fa-tokens JSON payloads? Unlikely. Also a log line where the fa-tokens JSON appears mid-line with a timestamp prefix — `.*$` handles prefix fine. What about a line where fa-tokens JSON is followed by something else on the same line from log interleaving? Would be skipped silently. Acceptable.

   Edge: JSON containing `}` inside string values, e.g. `"sessionId":"a}b"`. Greedy takes to last `}` which would be the string's closing... actually last `}` in the line is the final one if valid JSON. Fine for typical shapes.

   More subtle: `fa-tokens:` appearing in the middle of a longer JSON-like line where the captured group starts at the first `{` — greedy `.*` would swallow to the last `}` and JSON.parse could fail (returning null → returns null → tokens sample lost). E.g., a wrapper `{"msg":"fa-tokens: {...}"}` — the regex would match `fa-tokens: ` then capture `{...}"}` — the greedy match from the first `{` after `fa-tokens: `... Hmm, `text.match(/fa-tokens:\s*(\{.*\})\s*$/)` requires `fa-tokens:` then optional whitespace then `{`, and end at line end. In a wrapper line, after `{...}` there'd be `"}` at the end — `(\{.*\})` greedy takes everything from first `{` to last `}` at the line end, which would be the wrapper's closing brace, producing invalid JSON → parseJson returns null → return null. Then falls through? No — `return null` inside the `if (faMatch)` block. So a wrapped fa-tokens line yields null and the old `Tokens` check is skipped. Minor robustness issue, worth a suggestion at most. Actually it returns null and never reaches the CommandLineUtils branch — slight behavioral quirk. Low severity.

2. **`parseInt(payload.input, 10) || 0`** — if input is a float like 722300.5, parseInt truncates — fine. If input is a string with commas "722,300" → parseInt gives 722 — the old branch has parseNumberWithSuffix handling commas. fa emits raw numbers presumably. Minor.

3. **requests merging change**: Old code: `samples.push(Object.assign({ attemptIndex: samples.length + 1 }, lastRequests || {}, tokens));` — lastRequests always merged (stale metadata concern). New: `if (tokens.requests == null && lastRequests)` — but fa branch ALWAYS sets `requests: parseInt(...) || 0`, so tokens.requests is never null for fa lines. For CommandLineUtils branch, tokens.requests is undefined → merged. OK matches PR description.

   But wait — there's a subtle bug: for the fa branch, `requests: parseInt(payload.requests, 10) || 0` means if requests is missing it's 0, and `tokens.requests == null` is false (it's 0), so no merge. Fine.

4. **Dedup by (sessionId, segment) with `parseInt(payload.segment, 10) || 0`**: If segment is missing/0 for multiple lines of the same sessionId, all collapse to `session:0` and only first counted. Also if fa emits `segment:0` legitimately... Dedup keyed only on faSessionId when segment missing → repeated lines with same sessionId and no segment get dropped. Acceptable given the ledger format always has segment.

   More important: `faSegment: parseInt(payload.segment, 10) || 0` — a payload with segment legitimately 0 vs missing is indistinguishable. Minor.

   Another consideration: **dedup across multiple jobs/logs in the same run**. downloadRunLogs joins multiple jobs' logs with '\n'. If the same fa-tokens line legitimately appears in two jobs (e.g. setup job and main job echo the same ledger), dedup drops the second. That's the intent ("replayed"). OK.

   What about a run with TWO different fa sessions (resume creates new session? no — resume-aware means same sessionId, segment N increments). OK.

Mixed old+fa → only fa sources counted, source could be 'reported' even though some samples are old-style. Acceptable-ish. But note: aggregate `source` for a run mixing old and new would say 'reported' which is fine.

Note: cache — the usage cache stores `row` objects without `source` for older cached entries; when rendering from cache, old rows just have empty source. Fine.

If the same session's segments are split across separate extract calls (one per job log), extractTokenUsage is called on the joined logs so it's fine.

Wait no — `return null` inside the `if (faMatch)` block — the function returns null entirely, skipping old parsing. Is that right? A malformed fa-tokens line would be ignored rather than parsed by the old branch. The old branch requires "Tokens" substring anyway; "fa-tokens:" contains "tokens" but `indexOf('Tokens')` is case-sensitive — 'fa-tokens' lowercase wouldn't match 'Tokens'. So old branch wouldn't parse it anyway. Fine.

💡 **SUGGESTION: any unknown `source` value renders as the green "reported" badge**

The badge class is binary:

```javascript
(r.source === 'estimated' ? 'src-est' : 'src-rep')
```

If fa ever introduces a third source value (or a payload carries an unexpected/empty-ish string), the dashboard will show it with the solid green "reported" styling — visually asserting it is provider-reported when it is not. Since `source` is rendered verbatim inside the badge (`htmlEscape(r.source)`), a typo'd value would also display as-is.

Consider a small whitelist so only the known semantics get colored, e.g.:

```javascript
var srcClass = r.source === 'estimated' ? 'src-est' : (r.source === 'reported' ? 'src-rep' : 'src-unknown');
```

…plus a neutral `.src-unknown` style (or no badge at all for unrecognized values).

💡 **SUGGESTION: no test covers the "stale `lastRequests` no longer merged into fa lines" behavior**

The PR description calls out as a key decision: *"fa lines carry their own `requests`, so stale `lastRequests` metadata is no longer merged into them."* The mechanism is the new guard in `extractTokenUsage`:

```javascript
if (tokens.requests == null && lastRequests) base = Object.assign(base, lastRequests);
```

…but none of the four new tests exercises it. Since the fa branch always sets `requests` (coercing to `0` when absent), a regression that reverts to unconditional merging would pass the current suite while re-introducing the exact bug this PR fixes. A compact test:

```javascript
var usage = reporter.extractTokenUsage([
    'Requests 99 (pro)',
    'fa-tokens: {"sessionId":"s1","segment":1,"input":100,"output":10,"cacheRead":5,"requests":3,"source":"reported"}'
].join('\n'));
assert.equal(usage.requests, 3);          // not 99 + 3
assert.equal(usage.attempts[0].requestTier, '');
```

Also worth one assertion that an fa line **without** `requests` yields `requests: 0` rather than inheriting the stale value, to pin the intended semantics either way.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.

Tests pass (1583/0). Now let me do a thorough review.

Findings to consider:

1. **Regex `/fa-tokens:\s*(\{.*\})\s*$/`** — greedy `.*` with `$` anchor. On a line like `fa-tokens: {...} some trailing text` it won't match (good). But greedy `.*` matches to the LAST `}` on the line — if the JSON contains a nested `}` followed by trailing text... The `$` anchor requires the match to end at the end of the line (minus trailing whitespace). Since `(\{.*\})` must end with `}` immediately before `\s*$`, greedy matching takes the last `}` that allows the whole pattern to match. If the line is `prefix fa-tokens: {"a":1} garbage` — no match since after last `}` there's " garbage" which doesn't match `\s*$`. But wait: greedy backtracks — it could try `{"a":1}` and then require `\s*$` — " garbage" fails. So no match. Fine.

   Edge case: a line with TWO fa-tokens JSON payloads? Unlikely. Also a log line where the fa-tokens JSON appears mid-line with a timestamp prefix — `.*$` handles prefix fine. What about a line where fa-tokens JSON is followed by something else on the same line from log interleaving? Would be skipped silently. Acceptable.

   Edge: JSON containing `}` inside string values, e.g. `"sessionId":"a}b"`. Greedy takes to last `}` which would be the string's closing... actually last `}` in the line is the final one if valid JSON. Fine for typical shapes.

   More subtle: `fa-tokens:` appearing in the middle of a longer JSON-like line where the captured group starts at the first `{` — greedy `.*` would swallow to the last `}` and JSON.parse could fail (returning null → returns null → tokens sample lost). E.g., a wrapper `{"msg":"fa-tokens: {...}"}` — the regex would match `fa-tokens: ` then capture `{...}"}` — the greedy match from the first `{` after `fa-tokens: `... Hmm, `text.match(/fa-tokens:\s*(\{.*\})\s*$/)` requires `fa-tokens:` then optional whitespace then `{`, and end at line end. In a wrapper line, after `{...}` there'd be `"}` at the end — `(\{.*\})` greedy takes everything from first `{` to last `}` at the line end, which would be the wrapper's closing brace, producing invalid JSON → parseJson returns null → return null. Then falls through? No — `return null` inside the `if (faMatch)` block. So a wrapped fa-tokens line yields null and the old `Tokens` check is skipped. Minor robustness issue, worth a suggestion at most. Actually it returns null and never reaches the CommandLineUtils branch — slight behavioral quirk. Low severity.

2. **`parseInt(payload.input, 10) || 0`** — if input is a float like 722300.5, parseInt truncates — fine. If input is a string with commas "722,300" → parseInt gives 722 — the old branch has parseNumberWithSuffix handling commas. fa emits raw numbers presumably. Minor.

3. **requests merging change**: Old code: `samples.push(Object.assign({ attemptIndex: samples.length + 1 }, lastRequests || {}, tokens));` — lastRequests always merged (stale metadata concern). New: `if (tokens.requests == null && lastRequests)` — but fa branch ALWAYS sets `requests: parseInt(...) || 0`, so tokens.requests is never null for fa lines. For CommandLineUtils branch, tokens.requests is undefined → merged. OK matches PR description.

   But wait — there's a subtle bug: for the fa branch, `requests: parseInt(payload.requests, 10) || 0` means if requests is missing it's 0, and `tokens.requests == null` is false (it's 0), so no merge. Fine.

4. **Dedup by (sessionId, segment) with `parseInt(payload.segment, 10) || 0`**: If segment is missing/0 for multiple lines of the same sessionId, all collapse to `session:0` and only first counted. Also if fa emits `segment:0` legitimately... Dedup keyed only on faSessionId when segment missing → repeated lines with same sessionId and no segment get dropped. Acceptable given the ledger format always has segment.

   More important: `faSegment: parseInt(payload.segment, 10) || 0` — a payload with segment legitimately 0 vs missing is indistinguishable. Minor.

   Another consideration: **dedup across multiple jobs/logs in the same run**. downloadRunLogs joins multiple jobs' logs with '\n'. If the same fa-tokens line legitimately appears in two jobs (e.g. setup job and main job echo the same ledger), dedup drops the second. That's the intent ("replayed"). OK.

   What about a run with TWO different fa sessions (resume creates new session? no — resume-aware means same sessionId, segment N increments). OK.

5. **`source` aggregation**: `faSources` collected from samples with `sample.source` truthy. Old CommandLineUtils lines have no `source` → run source = '' when only old lines. Mixed old+fa → only fa sources counted, source could be 'reported' even though some samples are old-style. Acceptable-ish. But note: aggregate `source` for a run mixing old and new would say 'reported' which is fine.

   Edge: source value not 'reported'/'estimated' (e.g. something else) → badge CSS class: `r.source === 'estimated' ? 'src-est' : 'src-rep'` — any unknown source gets green 'reported' styling. And rowClass: only 'estimated' gets tint. Minor, suggestion-level.

6. **HTML**: `sourceBadge` uses htmlEscape(r.source) — good. `sortAttr(r.source || '')` escaped. OK.

7. **CSV**: `source` column added before `url`. Backward compat: consumers parsing CSV positionally would break, but CSV is header-based. Fine. Note: cache — the usage cache stores `row` objects without `source` for older cached entries; when rendering from cache, old rows just have empty source. Fine.

   One real issue: **cache invalidation**. Cached rows (from cache.json written before this change) lack `source`, so dashboard shows blank source for them until cache refresh. Not blocking.

8. **Test in PR description claims "1583 passed / 0 failed, including 4 new tests"** — verified: 1583 passed locally. ✓

9. **Ticket AC #2**: "Aggregation: sum segments per sessionId ... do not double-count resumed segments" — the implementation dedupes by (sessionId, segment) but note the semantics: it doesn't "sum per sessionId" — it sums all samples. If the same session's segments are split across separate extract calls (one per job log), extractTokenUsage is called on the joined logs so it's fine.

   Hmm wait — there's a real potential bug: **the same sessionId could legitimately emit the same segment number in different RUNS**, but extractTokenUsage is per-run, so no cross-run contamination. Good.

   Another real one: within a run, if fa is run twice with the same sessionId resumed across... covered.

10. **`attemptIndex` after `continue` on dedup**: `attemptIndex: samples.length + 1` — consistent.

11. **`fa-tokens:` check order**: The fa branch runs before the `Tokens` substring check. If a CommandLineUtils line contained "fa-tokens:" substring it would be misrouted — very unlikely.

12. **The old-line `requests` behavior change**: Previously `lastRequests` was always merged into tokens samples (even if the tokens line had its own requests? Old tokens lines don't have requests). New condition `tokens.requests == null` — old lines have undefined requests → merge happens. Same behavior. ✓

13. **resumeStages/feedback loop** — untouched.

14. **`payload.input == null && output == null && cacheRead == null` check** — if a line has only `requests` and `source` but no token fields, returns null and does NOT fall through to the old parser (returns null from within the faMatch block). Wait no — `return null` inside the `if (faMatch)` block — the function returns null entirely, skipping old parsing. Is that right? A malformed fa-tokens line would be ignored rather than parsed by the old branch. The old branch requires "Tokens" substring anyway; "fa-tokens:" contains "tokens" but `indexOf('Tokens')` is case-sensitive — 'fa-tokens' lowercase wouldn't match 'Tokens'. So old branch wouldn't parse it anyway. Fine.

15. **`rawTokensLine: text.trim()`** — includes full JSON. Fine.

16. Test quality: The tests are decent. The IT-7 fixture test covers parsing. Aggregation test covers dedup + mixed source. Dashboard test asserts string presence. CSV test asserts header contains 'source' and body contains 'reported' — weak-ish (could false positive) but fine.

(r.source === 'estimated' ? 'src-est' : 'src-rep')

Since `source` is rendered verbatim inside the badge (`htmlEscape(r.source)`), a typo'd value would also display as-is.

Consider a small whitelist so only the known semantics get colored, e.g.:

```javascript
var srcClass = r.source === 'estimated' ? 'src-est' : (r.source === 'reported' ? 'src-rep' : 'src-unknown');
```

…plus a neutral `.src-unknown` style (or no badge at all for unrecognized values).
